synthetic_confirmation.question: Does the E3 event-memory benefit survive genuinely held-out situations?
synthetic_confirmation.checkpoint_policy: reuse all 25 final E3 checkpoints, including seed 89; no best-checkpoint selection
synthetic_confirmation.episode_contract: one assigned lag per episode, exactly one question for each of four tasks
synthetic_confirmation.baseline_selection: highest E3 non-event development mean; chosen before any new held-out access
blockers: Implement and audit new shortcut-resistant held-out families; current E3 TEST path falls back to older single-object templates.
Review the proposed rectangular episode/cohort restriction and nested-bootstrap sensitivity to shared worlds.
Freeze dataset novelty checks, query identities, source hashes and checkpoint hashes before evaluation.
Implement checkpoint-loading evaluation and verify vocabulary/entity-slot compatibility without fitting on test.
Complete matched-resource and checkpoint-provenance audits; statistics alone cannot pass G1.
Obtain a separate execution and held-out-access authorization.

sherlock_dense_development.question: Does human event grouping improve recall-to-story retrieval with equal vector storage?
sherlock_dense_development.encoding_policy: encode each atomic description and development query once from text only; normalize atomic vectors, mean-pool per record, normalize again
sherlock_dense_development.storage: one float32 vector and two uint32 span bounds per record; no record source text is returned to a model
sherlock_dense_development.retrieval: common dot-product ranking of normalized vectors; chronological tie break
sherlock_dense_development.primary_metric: participant-macro maximum-IoU-target hit@5, retained from the v2 development protocol
sherlock_dense_development.primary_contrast: human_events minus mean of ten random-matched groupings; fixed chunks always reported
blockers: Select and pin one frozen text encoder and tokenizer revision without a result-based model search.
Freeze a long-query/atomic-text policy with no silent truncation and report its coverage.
Build provenance-checked embedding cache and cluster-only runner that excludes sealed subjects before encoding.
Audit the original source files and text/vector identity mapping; do not alter the v1/v2 results.
Add participant-level paired uncertainty, averaging random groupings within participant rather than treating ten groupings as ten people.
Review the remaining human-scene target-alignment bias; this is development retrieval evidence, not human recall prediction.
Obtain separate execution authorization; sealed five-person test remains closed.
